prs.title: feat(pnpr): store only the zstd tar for hosted tar registries
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements pnpm/tasks#226 for hosted registries that declare `tarballs: tar`. Such a registry is only ever served as tars, so the published `.tgz` had no reader there.

- **Publish:** the `.tgz` is verified against `dist.integrity` and its tar hash recorded, as before. pnpr then stores only the tar, compressed with zstd at level 19 within the window pnpm decodes, as `<name>-<version>.tar.zst`. A `.tgz` that doesn't decode in full fails with a 400, since there would be nothing to store.
- **Serve:** `GET <name>@<version>` returns the stored bytes to a `zstd` client. Any other client gets the tar decoded on a blocking thread, and the compression layer gzips it when asked. These versions skip the per-replica level-19 variant cache.
- **Config:** loading refuses a router without `tarballs: tar` that lists such a registry as a source, because it would have no `.tgz` to serve.
- **Lifecycle:**
  - Unpublish and packument rewrites remove the stored tar.
  - `pnpr verify` counts the stored tar as the version's blob, so `--prune-orphans` doesn't delete it. It skips the hash check for it, because `dist.integrity` names the `.tgz`.
  - `pnpr export` writes the stored tar.
- **Not covered:** the other half of the task, an optional zstd copy next to the `.tgz` for mixed registries.

The packument keeps the published `dist.integrity`, which stays the key into the tar-integrity table, so the tar registry view is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(deps-restorer): write links from the real path of a symlinked node_modules
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17448.

If a project's `node_modules` was a symlink (for example to another project's `node_modules`), pnpm v12 computed the relative targets of direct-dependency and hoisted links from the symlink's path. The OS resolves those links from the real directory. With the global virtual store, every link the install recreated pointed one or more `../` too high and dangled, yet the install exited 0.

The fix adds `pnpm_fs::symlinked_dir_real_path(base, dir)`. It returns the real path of `dir` only when a symlink lies between `base` and `dir`. The linker now uses that real path when it writes:

- direct-dependency links (base: the project directory),
- public and private hoist links (base: the lockfile directory's modules parent).

Ordinary layouts keep their lexical link contents. The `.bin` claim map and the `publishDirectory` modules-link cleanup still use the lexical modules dir.

pnpm v11 is not affected. It resolves each project's modules dir with `realpathMissing` (`installing/read-projects-context`). I ran the issue's reproduction against v11.28.9, and against a variant where the link is missing before the nested install. The links stayed valid in both.

## Summary

Running the Create Release PR workflow with only get-pnpm checked also bumped pnpm v12 (`pacquet`) and `@pnpm/napi`, and consumed every pending pacquet changeset (pnpm/pnpm#17458).

- before: `get-pnpm 0.0.10 → 0.0.11`, plus `pacquet` and `@pnpm/napi` `12.16.1 → 12.17.0`
- after: `get-pnpm 0.0.10 → 0.0.11` only

prs.title: fix(gvs): hash a dependency cycle as one unit
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17466.

With the global virtual store, a package in a dependency cycle kept its slot when a dependency of its cycle partner changed, and kept linking the partner's old slot. The project and the cycle then loaded two copies of the partner. The cause is how both graph hashers broke a cycle: a node that re-entered through its own ancestor was hashed with its children truncated, so the member reached second covered its partner by id only.

Both hashers (`pnpm/crates/graph-hasher` and `pnpm11/deps/graph-hasher`) now find the strongly connected components of the deps graph and hash each cycle as one unit. The fix is in both stacks because the two CLIs share one store.

- A node outside any cycle keeps `hash({ id, deps })`.
- Each cycle member starts with a label `hash({ id, deps })` over its children outside the cycle. Labels are refined with `hash({ color, deps })` over the children inside the cycle until a round no longer splits a group. This keeps one package in two peer contexts within one cycle on separate slots, unless their unrolled trees are identical.
- A member's digest is `hash({ member: label, component: hash(shape) })`, where `shape` maps each label to its in-cycle children's labels.

This differs from the issue's sketch in one way: members are identified by refined labels instead of by `fullPkgId`, since two members of one cycle can share a `fullPkgId`.

Fixes the repeat-install regression from pnpm/pnpm#17030. With a pnpmfile `readPackage` hook that changes a workspace project's dependencies, a repeat `pnpm install` never reported "Already up to date".

The cause: the install has two views of the project manifests, declared and hooked. Both had the same type, so callers kept passing the wrong one. Related to [pnpm/tasks#67](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/67). This PR takes the narrow fix rather than the config rebuild that task proposes.

When pnpm v12 installs the pnpm version a project pins, it passed the project's `supportedArchitectures` to that install. ## Summary

`--env-file` (pnpm/pnpm#16570, first shipped in v12.16.0) parsed its files with `dotenvy`. That expanded `$VAR` and rejected values Node.js accepts:
- Expansion ended a name at `_`, so `$T_BASE` became `$T` followed by `_BASE`.
- Windows paths, unquoted values with spaces, and `"cost $5"` failed the whole file.

Files load exactly as `node --env-file` loads them, with one exception: a leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is still dropped. Node.js keeps it as part of the first key, which gives a variable nobody can reference.

The PR started as a dotenvy replacement with its own syntax. It was reworked after review to match Node.js instead.

prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17465.

pnpm 12 kept regressing in how it treats the processes a script leaves running (#14356, #16628, #17465). pnpm 12 applied a multi-task orchestrator's policy to every command, so a single `pnpm exec` or `pnpm run` that failed, or that the user stopped with Ctrl+C, killed everything the script had started. That included a browser opened with the `open` package.

This PR writes the behaviour down as one contract, [`pnpm/crates/executor/PROCESS_LIFETIME.md`](pnpm/crates/executor/PROCESS_LIFETIME.md). The rule is that what a command leaves running outlives pnpm exactly when it would outlive the command run without pnpm. Cargo, `turbo exec`, npm, `deno task`, just, and moon follow the same rule. pnpm differs from it in two stated places:

1. When pnpm itself is killed or crashes, what it started ends with it, within each platform's limits.
2. When a task fails under bail, pnpm stops the tasks still running.
   - Unix: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a two-second grace.
   - Windows: a per-task Job Object is terminated.

Each row of the contract names the tests that pin it. Most of them are in `pnpm/crates/cli/tests/suite/process_lifetime/`, and many are differential: the fixture runs both directly and under pnpm, and the same leftovers must survive both runs. `pnpm/AGENTS.md` makes the contract binding for future changes. Every exit goes through `pnpm_executor::exit`, and `clippy.toml` bans `std::process::exit`.

prs.title: refactor(fs): make the copy permissions one type on every target
prs.author: KSXGitHub
prs.body:
## Summary

`CopyPermissions` was a type alias standing for two unrelated types: `std::fs::Permissions` off WASI, and a bare `u32` on it, because WASI metadata omits the permission bits and the host supplies the mode instead. Callers therefore branched on the target to say the same thing twice. From `cmd-shim`, before:

```rust
#[cfg(unix)]
let permissions = Permissions::from_mode(0o755);
#[cfg(target_os = "wasi")]
let permissions = 0o755;
Sys::set_permissions(path, permissions)
```

The same file's `FsSetPermissions` trait had a parameter whose type changed with the target, and two files aliased the one name over the other with `use pnpm_fs::CopyPermissions as Permissions;` — the shadowing that an alias over `std::fs::Permissions` invites.

It is a newtype now, wrapping what each platform's own calls hand over: the permission bits where a platform has them, the read-only attribute on Windows, which is the whole of `fs::Permissions` there. One vocabulary on every target: `of_metadata` and `copy_permissions` to read, `from_mode` and `mode` for the bits, `apply_to_file` and `apply_to_path` to write. The platform difference lives in one module, and the callers name one type. The same site becomes:

```rust
Sys::set_permissions(path, Permissions::from_mode(0o755))
```

prs.title: fix(install): relink a missing workspace dependency on a repeat install
prs.author: snmsoodan
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17485.

`pnpm install` answered "Already up to date" and left a declared `workspace:` dependency unlinked after its `node_modules` entry was deleted. Both the Rust v12 CLI and the TypeScript v11 CLI are affected (the issue reproduces on 12.16.1 and 11.28.9).

The repeat-install fast path in both stacks already stood down for a direct dependency link whose target was gone, but treated a missing entry as healthy, because skipped optional and excluded registry dependencies legitimately have none. It now also stands down when a local link the last install made is gone.

A missing entry counts only when all of these hold, so healthy layouts keep the fast path:

- **The manifest declares a `workspace:` or `link:` spec.** A cheap prefilter. Registry dependencies are never flagged.
- **No candidate entry holds the link.** The hoisted linker may place a sibling's dependency in the root modules directory. Under `dedupeDirectDeps` with a shared lockfile the root's link stands in for a sibling's. A root entry counts only when it resolves to the same target (same alias in v12, any alias the root importer links in v11, matching each linker's dedupe rule). The target the manifest names (the `link:` path or the workspace project's directory) is tried first, so a healthy deduped or hoisted sibling needs no lockfile read.
- **The lockfile links it.** The importer must record the alias with a `link:` version. The declared spec is not enough: an override (`lib: '-'`)

prs.title: fix(cmd-shim): run a .cmd bin when MSYS argument conversion is off
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

The sh shim for a `.cmd`/`.bat` bin started an interactive cmd.exe under Git Bash when MSYS argument conversion was off (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` or `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*'`), because it passed cmd a doubled `//C`. The shim now passes `/C` and excludes it from conversion through `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL`, as the issue proposes. Fixed in both pnpm v12 (`pnpm/crates/cmd-shim`) and v11 (`pnpm11/bins/cmd-shim`, `pnpm11/bins/linker`).

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17480

Trade-off for review: an `MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL` entry excludes every argument that starts with it, case-sensitively. The shim upper-cases the first standalone `/c` or `/k`, the switch that ends cmd.exe's own switches, before excluding it, so Git Bash drive paths such as `/c/Users` still convert. With conversion on, a user argument starting with uppercase `/C` or `/K` is no longer converted. The exported variable is also inherited by cmd.exe and what the batch file runs.

prs.title: fix(runtime): choose stable Node.js latest releases
prs.author: kairosci
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17490. `pnpm runtime set node latest` (and `pnpm env use latest`, `pnpm env list latest`, `pnpm pack-app` with `latest`, `pnpm outdated` for runtime deps) picked the first entry of the Node.js release index, which can be a prerelease such as `27.0.0-alpha.0.0.0`. Both CLIs had the bug.

The Node.js resolvers in v11 and v12 now resolve `latest` to the newest stable entry of the index. When the index has no stable entry, as on the `nightly` or `rc` channel, `latest` still picks the first entry, so `node@nightly` resolves to the newest nightly. The resolver signatures are unchanged.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
Resolve the Node.js `latest` selector to the newest stable entry of the
release index. When the index has no stable entry, which is what the
nightly, rc, and other prerelease channel indexes look like, fall back
to the first entry, so `node@nightly` keeps resolving to the newest
nightly build.

The fallback keeps the exported resolveNodeVersion/resolveNodeVersions
contract intact: callers that pass a prerelease mirror URL without a
release channel still get a version for `latest`.

Closes pnpm/pnpm#17490
```
